reason: Reads one page live from Notion, as drive-cli's documents get reads one live from Google; documents show is kept for the local copy that step 2 adds (docs/dev/DESIGN.md, Commands). Review when the vocabulary names a live read beside show.

A Notion database holds data sources of rows with typed properties; no shared noun names it, as sheets is Drive's own (docs/dev/DESIGN.md, Commands). Add it to the cli-base vocabulary if a second CLI gets databases (Airtable, Coda).

The link a child page gets before its text is read, in Notion's own form https://app.notion.com/p/{page-id} (src/sync/source.ts); a person opens it, notion never sends a request there, and hostFetch would refuse one.

Notion's own name for the switch its Markdown update takes (allow_deleting_content), and the flag of Notion's own CLI: it lets an update delete the child pages and databases its new text leaves out. The vocabulary's --allow-delete means a call that deletes for good, and Notion's API deletes no page for good (https://developers.notion.com/reference/trash-page; docs/dev/DESIGN.md, Writes). Add it to the cli-base vocabulary if a second CLI writes pages with children (Confluence, Outline).

Notion answers in a discussion by its discussion_id (https://developers.notion.com/reference/create-a-comment), as drive-cli's comments reply answers in a Google comment thread; review when the shared vocabulary names comment-thread actions.
Sends a local file to Notion's file uploads and adds it to a page, as drive-cli's files upload sends one to Drive; review when the shared vocabulary names an upload verb.
Notion's list comments takes only a page or block and a cursor (https://developers.notion.com/reference/list-comments); there is nothing to filter by on Notion's side.
